title: Merge Adjacent Piles
source: Classic interval-DP problem (stone merging). Included because partition/interval DP is repeatedly reported as the Infosys SP Hard-slot topic (e.g. Naukri Code360 SP experiences mentioning partition DP); not a verbatim Infosys question
statement:
A warehouse has `N` piles of crates in a single row; pile `i` contains `A[i]` crates.

In one operation you choose **two adjacent piles** and merge them into one pile (it takes their place in the row). The operation costs the total number of crates in the new pile.

You keep merging until a single pile remains. Print the minimum possible total cost.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `N`.
The second line contains `N` space-separated integers `A[1..N]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the minimum total cost (`0` if `N = 1`).

samples.explanation: Merge `4+1 = 5` (cost 5) → `5 3 2`; merge `3+2 = 5` (cost 5) → `5 5`; merge `5+5 = 10` (cost 10). Total `20`. Another optimal order is `1+3` (4), `4+2` (6), `4+6` (10). Merging `4+4` second would give `22`.
`10+1 = 11` (cost 11), then `11+10 = 21` (cost 21) → `32`. Merging the other side first is symmetric.

hints: Think about the **very last** merge: it joins a pile made from `A[i..m]` with a pile made from `A[m+1..j]`. Its cost is always `sum(A[i..j])`, whatever happened before.
So the cost to fully merge a range `[i, j]` = best split point `m` + the cost of each side + the range sum. Ranges depend only on strictly shorter ranges.
`dp[i][j] = min_{i ≤ m < j} (dp[i][m] + dp[m+1][j]) + prefix[j+1] − prefix[i]`, `dp[i][i] = 0`. Fill by increasing length.
editorial:
### State
`dp[i][j]` = minimum cost to merge piles `i..j` (inclusive) into one pile.

### Transition
The final merge of the range combines `[i..m]` and `[m+1..j]` for some `m`:
`dp[i][j] = min_{m=i}^{j-1} (dp[i][m] + dp[m+1][j]) + S(i, j)`
where `S(i, j)` is the range sum, obtained in `O(1)` from prefix sums.

### Base case
`dp[i][i] = 0` (a single pile needs no merge).

### Order
By increasing range length `2..N`; every needed sub-range is shorter.

### Answer
`dp[0][N-1]`.

### Complexity
`O(N^3 / 6)` ≈ `1.3·10^6` for `N = 200`, `O(N^2)` memory.

### Common mistakes
- Greedy "always merge the cheapest adjacent pair" - not optimal for adjacent-only merging (it is optimal only when any two piles may be merged, i.e. Huffman).
- Iterating `i` and `j` in plain nested loops (`dp[m+1][j]` not ready yet) instead of by length.
- Forgetting the range sum is added once per merge level.
